issues.main_description_html:
Design and frontend integration for Direction Route Section Redesign, per:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-route-panel-redesign/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-route-panel-redesign/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/direction-route

MapThru finds routes well but explains them poorly: the result is a plain text list with no icons, no floor context, no distance and no visual order, it shows nothing at all when the trip stays on one floor, and no step can be pressed to see where it happens on the map. This redesigns the route result inside the Direction panel into four parts — status, summary, step timeline and step interaction — and adds a compact layout for small screens and embedded projects.

Scope

  • Status — a short line confirming a route, or a plain-language reason when none was found, still naming buildings that have no usable door.
  • Summary — origin and destination, floor changes, building count and step count, plus total distance and estimated walking time when the project has a real floor plan scale. Zero counts are omitted; a dropped-pin origin is described in words.
  • Step timeline — vertical, in travel order, with connectors and a type icon per step (walk, take lift, take stairs, go outside, arrive). Floor context on floor changes, building name on cross-building steps, per-step distance on every walking step in scaled projects. Every found route shows a first walking step and a final arrival step, including single-floor routes.
  • Step interaction — selecting a step switches floor when needed, focuses the map on that leg and highlights it; selecting again or clearing returns to the whole route. Selection never changes origin, destination or route, and is cleared on recalculation. The outdoor step focuses without forcing a floor change.
  • Compact layout — small screens and embedded projects keep status and summary always visible, allow the step list to collapse (expanded on first result), reduce row density and scroll long lists inside the section.
  • Distance and time rule — shown only for scaled projects. Unscaled projects show no distance, no time, no placeholder, no plan-unit fallback and no prompt. Pace is 1.2 m/s product-wide, plus 60s per lift transfer and 30s per floor of stairs.

Out of scope: turn-by-turn navigation, live positioning, route preferences, waypoints, saving/sharing routes, routing-engine changes, a new backend API, a floor-plan-scale control, and any change to the To/From inputs, drop pin mode or Search/Building/Floor/Information/Event behavior.
